work.title: Human-only decisions are one click in the dashboard: the operator signs in as a human, and each request offers ready-made choices

criteria.text: The human operator signs into the dashboard as a human without handling tokens: `graphyard login` (or the installer at the end of an install) prints a one-time sign-in link that creates a human admin session in the browser (short-lived, single use, bound to the operator principal), and the dashboard shows which identity is signed in. A card that the current session cannot answer says why and offers 'Sign in as the operator' instead of a CLI command. A test asserts the link is single-use, expires, grants the admin human session, and that a reader or agent session sees the sign-in action rather than a command.

Every human-only request carries structured choices chosen by the requester (e.g. for money-or-accounts: 'Approve up to €X/month', 'Approve with a different cap…', 'Decline'; for credentials: 'Provide now' with a secure input sealed to the host, 'Decline'), each a button, with an optional note. The park command and the loop's own requests accept these choices; an answer records the choice and the note. The CLI remains available but is never shown as the primary path. A browser test answers a money request with one click and asserts the recorded choice, at desktop and 375 px.
docs/dashboard.md states the sign-in link and the choice buttons within the docs word budget.

Every installation declares its operator principal a human session (sessionKind "human" in GRAPHYARD_PRINCIPALS) at install time, and `graphyard master principals` keeps it on rotation, so human-only requests are answerable from the first day. On 2026-09-26 no principal was declared human, so no human-only request (GY-73) could be answered by anyone. A test runs the install plan and a rotation and asserts the operator principal is declared human and no agent principal is. The item creates browser-tests/human-decisions.spec.ts for its dashboard tests.

work.title: Land prodfix/secrets-bus: confined sessions push through a keyring-only D-Bus proxy

criteria.text: With a live proxy socket, processLaunchMaskWords binds it over each session-bus socket; with no socket, a regular file or a relative path it binds /dev/null; secretsBusPath honours GRAPHYARD_SECRETS_BUS, then XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, then /run/user/<uid>.
A confined shell still cannot write, commit in or switch the coordinator checkout, and systemd-run --user is still refused inside the namespace, with or without the proxy running.

The item creates deploy/systemd/graphyard-secrets-bus.service, which runs the filtered proxy, and docs/master-agent-sessions.md states that the session bus becomes the keyring-only proxy when it runs; `npm run build` and `npm test` pass.

work.title: A launch whose supervisor is still setting up counts as starting, not absent, so a slow control plane does not fail healthy launches at 60 s

work.title: Follow-ups from the approved review of GY-888 (PR #455)

judgement.reason: Real, unfixed P1 containment hole. At PR #455's head d13fee0482 (= the approved review commit; no later code change), src/master/profiles.ts:650 readOnlyMountWrapper hard-codes gitDir = join(root, '.git') and drops every shared re-bind that is not a directory (.filter(isDirectoryPath)); runtimeSandboxConfines (line 572) and sessionGitAdminDirectory share the assumption. When the coordinator checkout is a linked worktree (a supported install mode per the repo's own worktree-install flow), <root>/.git is a pointer file: all shared re-binds resolve under a file and vanish, and the true common Git directory lies outside root, so --ro-bind root root never covers it while --dev-bind / / leaves it writable — a confined session can git -C <coordinator> commit --allow-empty and move the coordinator branch, voiding GY-888's guarantee. Not already fixed: the code exists only on the PR branch (origin/main has neither readOnlyMountWrapper nor sessionGitAdminDirectory) and thread PRRT_kwDOUZby-s6m_HFI (r4130348375) was resolved by a reply naming this item, not by code. Not mergeable into GY-888: the reviewer approved it with all criteria met and judged this finding beyond the item's criteria, matching the repo's follow-up-item convention (GY-936, GY-940, GY-952). Priority 1: P1 severity on a supported deployment path, actionable as GY-888 lands since the vulnerable code is not yet on main.

after.title: Follow-ups from the approved review of GY-888 (PR #455)

judgement.reason: Real, unfixed P1 containment hole. At PR #455's head d13fee0482 (= the approved review commit; no later code change), src/master/profiles.ts:650 readOnlyMountWrapper hard-codes gitDir = join(root, '.git') and drops every shared re-bind that is not a directory (.filter(isDirectoryPath)); runtimeSandboxConfines (line 572) and sessionGitAdminDirectory share the assumption. When the coordinator checkout is a linked worktree (a supported install mode per the repo's own worktree-install flow), <root>/.git is a pointer file: all shared re-binds resolve under a file and vanish, and the true common Git directory lies outside root, so --ro-bind root root never covers it while --dev-bind / / leaves it writable — a confined session can git -C <coordinator> commit --allow-empty and move the coordinator branch, voiding GY-888's guarantee. Not already fixed: the code exists only on the PR branch (origin/main has neither readOnlyMountWrapper nor sessionGitAdminDirectory) and thread PRRT_kwDOUZby-s6m_HFI (r4130348375) was resolved by a reply naming this item, not by code. Not mergeable into GY-888: the reviewer approved it with all criteria met and judged this finding beyond the item's criteria, matching the repo's follow-up-item convention (GY-936, GY-940, GY-952). Priority 1: P1 severity on a supported deployment path, actionable as GY-888 lands since the vulnerable code is not yet on main.

work.title: Blocked work unblocks itself: the loop re-checks each blocker's cause every cycle, frees the slot at once, and resolves the routine kinds without the master

criteria.text: Blocker text from the 2026-09-30 incidents (e.g. "could not read Username for https://github.com", "complete command failed with Internal error", "unable to append to '.git/logs/refs/remotes/...': Read-only file system", "SCOPE NEEDED: src/model/queue.ts ... 8106499e9f") is classified into the named classes, and unrecognised text is classed genuine; a unit test covers every class.

A worker attempt that records a blocker ends in the same transaction with partial work kept and the lease released, so the item holds no worker slot while blocked; a test shows the slot is free on the next dispatch.

For each environmental class the loop runs its probe each cycle (credential and sandbox probes inside the same confinement wrapper a worker gets) and unblocks the item with an audit record once the probe passes, and never while it fails; a test drives a failing then passing probe.

A planned-file-scope blocker naming files and a commit becomes an additive planned-files widening decision for an independent approver without master action, and a needs-decision blocker gets its approver launched; tests cover both.

master status and the board show each blocked item's class, last probe result and next probe time, and count only genuine or human-only classes as needing someone; `npm run build` and `npm test` pass and docs/master-agent.md describes the classes.

exercise.behaviour: classifyBlocker's class regex matching: every non-human-only blocker text short-circuited to the 'genuine' class (src/model/blocker-class.ts `if (!blocker) return genuine` made unconditional)

the engine's `blocked` command no longer ends the attempt: removed endAttempt(...,'released'), `work.lease = null`, `work.scopeRequest = null` and the interrupted capacity record with partialWork (src/engine.ts blocked branch)

the blocker step's environmental-class probe in src/daemon/cycle-blockers.ts (`if (environmentalBlockerClasses.includes(classification.class))` disabled), so the loop never probes or clears an environmental blocker
blockerScopeDecision removed from the decision chain in src/daemon/cycle-decisions.ts and the needs-decision approver launch in src/daemon/cycle-blockers.ts disabled
the board's blocker view in src/model/board.ts: routineBlocker next-actor, the routine-class null command, and the per-row `blocker: blockerView(entry)` field removed

work.title: Review findings are classified mechanical vs substantive: mechanical ones are auto-fixed by the worker bot before independent review

criteria.text: Review findings carry a classification: mechanical (typos, docs placement, formatting, naming-alignment with existing conventions) or substantive (behavior, criteria, scope). Mechanical findings on an otherwise-approved head are fixed by a worker-class bot commit before the independent reviewer's fresh read, so reviewers only ever see substance.

The classifier mislabeling a substantive finding as mechanical is caught: the reviewer still sees the full diff and can reject the bot commit, which records the misclassification as an intervention signal for the retro synthesis.

work.title: Most merge-queue conflicts are in a handful of shared docs pages, so every merge on main sends queued items back to a full worker rework

criteria.text: A candidate whose conflicts with the base are confined to docs/**/*.md is refreshed by the control plane, not reworked: a short docs-sync session (reviewer-class account, narrow prompt: merge the base, keep both sides' meaning, stay within the word budget, touch only the conflicted docs paragraphs) resolves it on the item's branch, the docs obligation check and word-budget test rerun, and the item keeps its approval when the non-docs diff (patch-id of paths outside docs/) is unchanged. A test asserts: a docs-only conflict leads to a docs-sync session and no rework decision; a conflict touching src/ still goes to rework; approval kept when the non-docs patch is unchanged.

master status and Insights report conflict hotspots: the paths most often conflicting in the last 24 hours with counts and the items they sent back, and raise an attention item when one path causes 5 or more conflicts in 24 hours. A test asserts the report.

docs/development.md states how to document a change so it rarely conflicts (add a self-contained paragraph or section rather than rewording shared sentences) and the docs-sync rule, within the docs word budget.

work.title: Most merge-queue conflicts are in a handful of shared docs pages, so every merge on main sends queued items back to a full worker rework

criteria.text: A candidate whose conflicts with the base are confined to docs/**/*.md is refreshed by the control plane, not reworked: a short docs-sync session (reviewer-class account, narrow prompt: merge the base, keep both sides' meaning, stay within the word budget, touch only the conflicted docs paragraphs) resolves it on the item's branch, the docs obligation check and word-budget test rerun, and the item keeps its approval when the non-docs diff (patch-id of paths outside docs/) is unchanged. A test asserts: a docs-only conflict leads to a docs-sync session and no rework decision; a conflict touching src/ still goes to rework; approval kept when the non-docs patch is unchanged.

master status and Insights report conflict hotspots: the paths most often conflicting in the last 24 hours with counts and the items they sent back, and raise an attention item when one path causes 5 or more conflicts in 24 hours. A test asserts the report.

docs/development.md states how to document a change so it rarely conflicts (add a self-contained paragraph or section rather than rewording shared sentences) and the docs-sync rule, within the docs word budget.

exercise.behaviour: docsOnlyConflict in src/model/docs-sync.ts stubbed to always return false, so a docs-only conflict is never routed to a docs-sync session; the proof failed (5 pass, 1 fail in the file)
conflictHotspots in src/model/conflict-hotspots.ts stubbed to return empty hotspots and attention lists, so no conflicting paths are reported or raised; the proof failed (5 pass, 1 fail in the file)

judgement.reason: Real, unfixed P1 containment hole. At PR #455's head d13fee0482 (= the approved review commit; no later code change), src/master/profiles.ts:650 readOnlyMountWrapper hard-codes gitDir = join(root, '.git') and drops every shared re-bind that is not a directory (.filter(isDirectoryPath)); runtimeSandboxConfines (line 572) and sessionGitAdminDirectory share the assumption. When the coordinator checkout is a linked worktree (a supported install mode per the repo's own worktree-install flow), <root>/.git is a pointer file: all shared re-binds resolve under a file and vanish, and the true common Git directory lies outside root, so --ro-bind root root never covers it while --dev-bind / / leaves it writable — a confined session can git -C <coordinator> commit --allow-empty and move the coordinator branch, voiding GY-888's guarantee. Not already fixed: the code exists only on the PR branch (origin/main has neither readOnlyMountWrapper nor sessionGitAdminDirectory) and thread PRRT_kwDOUZby-s6m_HFI (r4130348375) was resolved by a reply naming this item, not by code. Not mergeable into GY-888: the reviewer approved it with all criteria met and judged this finding beyond the item's criteria, matching the repo's follow-up-item convention (GY-936, GY-940, GY-952). Priority 1: P1 severity on a supported deployment path, actionable as GY-888 lands since the vulnerable code is not yet on main.

work.title: A new attempt's worktree never fails because an earlier attempt's worktree still holds the branch

criteria.text: Worktree allocation for a new attempt that finds the item's branch held by an earlier attempt's worktree (checked out, or mid rebase, merge or cherry-pick) records that worktree's refs and uncommitted diff under the item's preserved-attempt record, ends the in-progress operation, detaches that worktree's HEAD, and then creates the new worktree; the branch ref never moves. A test leaves a rebase in progress on the branch in an old attempt's worktree and asserts the next allocation succeeds with the branch at its prior commit and the old state recorded.

A dispatch that fails for a host-side reason about the item's own workspace (not the profile) neither advances the attempt epoch nor puts the profile into its failure cool-off; the failure is recorded on the item with the git message. The item creates tests/worktree-branch-lock.test.ts for these tests.

work.title: Automatic quarantine settlement bounds the clock with a fast read, not the slow snapshot

criteria.text: Before assessing containment, the loop measures its clock offset against the control plane with a light timed read whose round trip bounds the offset (the server's time from a small endpoint, or the Date of a cheap request), and passes those bounds to the assessment instead of the snapshot read's. A test with a 12-second snapshot read and a 200 ms timed read asserts a lapsed, verified-dead quarantine is settled automatically.

When the light read itself cannot bound the offset within tolerance, the refusal names the measured round trip, and master status says settlement waits on a faster control-plane read rather than on a clock disagreement. A test asserts the wording.

work.title: The loop requests rework for a CI failure that the base branch fails too, so approvers refuse a rework per item and nothing repairs main

criteria.text: Before requesting rework for a failed required check, the loop compares the failing test names on the candidate with the latest completed run of the same check on the base branch head (read outside any coordination transaction). A failure present on the base too is classified 'base failure': no rework is requested for it and no approver is launched. A test asserts: same failing test on base leads to no rework request; a failure only on the candidate leads to rework as today.

A base failure raises one attention item and one P0 work item per distinct failing test (deduplicated by test name and base head), naming the test, the base commit, the CI run and the candidates it blocks. When the base's check passes again, the attention clears and the blocked candidates get their failed jobs rerun. A test asserts: one item for three blocked candidates; attention cleared and reruns requested once main is green.
docs/master-agent.md states the base-failure rule within the docs word budget.

A CI rerun reuses the candidate's original merge commit, so it cannot clear a base failure the candidate carries in its own tree (2026-09-26: GY-368, GY-392, GY-418, GY-430, GY-446 and GY-264 kept the fixed-date test after PR #284 repaired main). Once the base check passes again, each candidate blocked by that base failure is refreshed onto the repaired base by a Graphyard-authored merge of the base into its branch, keeping its approval under the existing carry rules, and its CI runs on the refreshed head. A test asserts the refresh is made once per blocked candidate and the approval binding survives it.

exercise.behaviour: judgeFailedCheck stubbed to always return kind 'own', so a failure the base head shares is no longer classified a base failure
step 2 of baseFailureStep (filing the P0 item via fileBaseFailure) removed and baseFailureAttention made to return no lines
step 4 of baseFailureStep no longer calls effects.refreshCandidate for blocked candidates once the base passes

work.title: Concurrent agent test runs exhaust host memory: the loop launches sessions with no bound on full-suite and typecheck runs per machine

criteria.text: Heavy verification commands run under a per-host concurrency bound: `npm test`, `npm run test:browser` and `tsc --noEmit` launched by Graphyard sessions (worker, producer, reviewer) take a slot from a host-wide semaphore (a lock directory under the managed worktree root, default slots = max(2, floor(total memory GB / 8)), configurable per host) and wait for a free slot, printing that they wait and on what. Implemented as a wrapper the session harness puts on PATH for those commands (or the test runner itself acquiring the slot). judgement.reason: Real, unfixed P1 containment hole. At PR #455's head d13fee0482 (= the approved review commit; no later code change), src/master/profiles.ts:650 readOnlyMountWrapper hard-codes gitDir = join(root, '.git') and drops every shared re-bind that is not a directory (.filter(isDirectoryPath)); runtimeSandboxConfines (line 572) and sessionGitAdminDirectory share the assumption. When the coordinator checkout is a linked worktree (a supported install mode per the repo's own worktree-install flow), <root>/.git is a pointer file: all shared re-binds resolve under a file and vanish, and the true common Git directory lies outside root, so --ro-bind root root never covers it while --dev-bind / / leaves it writable — a confined session can git -C <coordinator> commit --allow-empty and move the coordinator branch, voiding GY-888's guarantee. Not already fixed: the code exists only on the PR branch (origin/main has neither readOnlyMountWrapper nor sessionGitAdminDirectory) and thread PRRT_kwDOUZby-s6m_HFI (r4130348375) was resolved by a reply naming this item, not by code. Not mergeable into GY-888: the reviewer approved it with all criteria met and judged this finding beyond the item's criteria, matching the repo's follow-up-item convention (GY-936, GY-940, GY-952). Priority 1: P1 severity on a supported deployment path, actionable as GY-888 lands since the vulnerable code is not yet on main.

work.title: Review, rework and proof launches require a GitHub observation under two minutes old, which the observation workers rarely supply, so items wait hours for a reviewer

criteria.text: A review, producer or approver launch requires only that the item's latest observation is of the request's exact head and base (no age bound); if the head or base has moved since, the request is superseded as today. The two-minute bound stays for merge authorization. A test with a 20-minute-old observation of the requested head asserts the review launches, and one of a moved head asserts it does not.

Where a fresh observation is genuinely required (merge, rework of a possibly-moved head), the requesting step wakes that item's observation job with priority immediately after the refusal, and the next attempt happens after that observation lands rather than on a fixed retry. A test asserts the wake and that the second attempt follows the observation.
master status reports, per waiting launch, how long it has waited and why; a review request waiting over 15 minutes raises an attention item. A test asserts it.

work.title: Candidates whose CI failed only from a since-fixed base-branch breakage are refreshed onto main automatically

criteria.text: When a candidate's required check fails and every failing test also fails on the base branch commit it was built against, while that test passes on the current base tip, the loop refreshes the candidate onto the base tip (the same refresh the merge queue uses, keeping approvals and proofs the refresh policy keeps) instead of requesting rework, and records why. A test builds this history (a failing test on the old base, fixed on the new tip) and asserts the refresh with no rework decision. The item creates src/master/base-break-refresh.ts for this detection and tests/base-break-refresh.test.ts for its tests.

A decision step gated on a fresh GitHub observation wakes that item's observation job itself and is re-evaluated as soon as the reading lands, so the freshness bound is met rather than missed on every cycle. A test asserts that a waiting rework decision proceeds within one observation after the wake, not on the next unrelated cycle.

master status names a candidate held only by a base-branch breakage as such (the failing test, the base commit that broke it and the one that fixed it), not as 'needs a new head'. A test asserts the wording.

work.title: Review, rework and proof launches require a GitHub observation under two minutes old, which the observation workers rarely supply, so items wait hours for a reviewer

criteria.text: A review, producer or approver launch requires only that the item's latest observation is of the request's exact head and base (no age bound); if the head or base has moved since, the request is superseded as today. The two-minute bound stays for merge authorization. A test with a 20-minute-old observation of the requested head asserts the review launches, and one of a moved head asserts it does not.

Where a fresh observation is genuinely required (merge, rework of a possibly-moved head), the requesting step wakes that item's observation job with priority immediately after the refusal, and the next attempt happens after that observation lands rather than on a fixed retry. A test asserts the wake and that the second attempt follows the observation.
master status reports, per waiting launch, how long it has waited and why; a review request waiting over 15 minutes raises an attention item. A test asserts it.

At PR #455's head d13fee0482 (= the approved review commit; no later code change), src/master/profiles.ts:650 readOnlyMountWrapper hard-codes gitDir = join(root, '.git') and drops every shared re-bind that is not a directory (.filter(isDirectoryPath)); runtimeSandboxConfines (line 572) and sessionGitAdminDirectory share the assumption. When the coordinator checkout is a linked worktree (a supported install mode per the repo's own worktree-install flow), <root>/.git is a pointer file: all shared re-binds resolve under a file and vanish, and the true common Git directory lies outside root, so --ro-bind root root never covers it while --dev-bind / / leaves it writable — a confined session can git -C <coordinator> commit --allow-empty and move the coordinator branch, voiding GY-888's guarantee. Not already fixed: the code exists only on the PR branch (origin/main has neither readOnlyMountWrapper nor sessionGitAdminDirectory) and thread PRRT_kwDOUZby-s6m_HFI (r4130348375) was resolved by a reply naming this item, not by code. Not mergeable into GY-888: the reviewer approved it with all criteria met and judged this finding beyond the item's criteria, matching the repo's follow-up-item convention (GY-936, GY-940, GY-952). Priority 1: P1 severity on a supported deployment path, actionable as GY-888 lands since the vulnerable code is not yet on main.

work.title: Candidates whose CI failed only from a since-fixed base-branch breakage are refreshed onto main automatically

criteria.text: When a candidate's required check fails and every failing test also fails on the base branch commit it was built against, while that test passes on the current base tip, the loop refreshes the candidate onto the base tip (the same refresh the merge queue uses, keeping approvals and proofs the refresh policy keeps) instead of requesting rework, and records why. A test builds this history (a failing test on the old base, fixed on the new tip) and asserts the refresh with no rework decision. The item creates src/master/base-break-refresh.ts for this detection and tests/base-break-refresh.test.ts for its tests.

A decision step gated on a fresh GitHub observation wakes that item's observation job itself and is re-evaluated as soon as the reading lands, so the freshness bound is met rather than missed on every cycle. A test asserts that a waiting rework decision proceeds within one observation after the wake, not on the next unrelated cycle.

master status names a candidate held only by a base-branch breakage as such (the failing test, the base commit that broke it and the one that fixed it), not as 'needs a new head'. A test asserts the wording.

work.title: A pipeline-doctor agent runs every 10 minutes, finds stuck and overdue work, and fixes it through sanctioned commands, doing what the master has done by hand all day

criteria.text: A 'doctor' agent role, implemented in a new module this item creates (src/daemon/doctor.ts), (registry and profile role, headless on Pi by default with a strong-model fallback, like the diagnostician) is launched by the loop every 10 minutes (configurable, run.doctor.intervalMinutes) with the master's read access and the operator-agent identity's sanctioned commands only (master scope, requirements, unblock, decide + approver, settle-containment, close, create/release), never merge, dispatch, evidence or lease commands. Its prompt is a shipped template (not this repository's session prompts) listing the checks and fault bounds: blocked > 10 min, worker > 60 min, CI > 20 min, review request > 5 min after green CI, launch > 2 min, proofs > 30 min, mergeable > 5 min, unanswered decision > 10 min, lapsed containment, stale refusal text, items overdue in any step. A test asserts the schedule, the role's command allowlist (a refused command is recorded, not run) and that the template names every bound.

Each doctor run records its findings and actions as an event per item and one run summary (what was stuck, why, what it did, what it filed), visible in master status and on the dashboard (a 'Doctor' panel with the last runs). A finding it cannot act on (a human-only decision, a fault class with no item) raises attention or files a P0/P1 fault item with criteria and plannedFiles, deduplicated against open items. A test asserts the event, the summary and the dedup.

The deterministic remedies the doctor applies most often are also performed by the loop itself without an agent: settle a lapsed containment whose attempt submitted; clear a blocker whose named scope is already in plannedFiles; relaunch an approver for a decision unanswered past 10 minutes. The doctor handles what needs judgement. A test asserts each automatic remedy.

docs/master-agent.md and docs/onboarding.md state the doctor role, its schedule, its command allowlist and how an installation turns it off, within the docs word budget; onboarding enables it by default.

work.title: OpenCode sessions never count as started: the start pattern /\bOpenCode\b/ never matches OpenCode 1.18's screen, so every OpenCode launch times out and silently falls back to Claude

criteria.text: The OpenCode start check in src/master/launch.ts recognizes OpenCode 1.18's start screen: the TUI's own elements, such as the input prompt or hint bar ('tab agents' / 'ctrl+' hints) or the logo drawn in box characters, and not the echoed launch command line, which also contains the lowercase word opencode. A test in tests/runtime-screens.test.ts feeds a recorded OpenCode 1.18 start screen (captured as a fixture) and asserts 'ready', and feeds the bare echoed launch command and asserts it is not ready.

When a launch falls back to another account after the preferred account's runtime failed to start, the dispatch record and master status name both (for example 'opencode-a failed to start: <reason>; launched on claude-b'), and three consecutive start failures of one account raise one attention item naming the account and runtime, so a runtime that never starts is visible rather than silently replaced. A test asserts the record, and that the attention item appears after three failures.

work.title: Headless Pi runs are children of the loop or executor process, so every restart kills them (exit 143) and their items lose the attempt

criteria.text: A headless run is started detached from the launching process (its own systemd transient scope or setsid process group, like `watch` workers), with its output and result written to its run record on disk. A restarted loop or executor re-adopts every run still live from the run registry: it keeps waiting on it and applies its result when it ends. Runs whose process is gone without a result are recorded as lost and retried without spending an attempt. A test starts a fake headless run, restarts the owning component (simulated), and asserts that the run survives, is re-adopted, and has its result applied exactly once.

A planned restart (self-upgrade GY-437, `master executors restart`, a systemd restart) never sends a signal to live headless runs, and the loop's shutdown hook logs how many runs it left running. A test asserts that shutdown leaves detached runs untouched.

exercise.behaviour: adoptRuns in src/runner/registry.ts stubbed to return [] at once: a restarted loop/executor no longer re-adopts live runs from the run registry on disk
detachRuns cancels (signals) each run instead of run.detach(), and runDaemon's shutdown 'stopping: left N headless run(s) running' log removed

work.title: Follow-ups from the approved review of GY-888 (PR #455)

judgement.reason: Real, unfixed P1 containment hole. At PR #455's head d13fee0482 (= the approved review commit; no later code change), src/master/profiles.ts:650 readOnlyMountWrapper hard-codes gitDir = join(root, '.git') and drops every shared re-bind that is not a directory (.filter(isDirectoryPath)); runtimeSandboxConfines (line 572) and sessionGitAdminDirectory share the assumption. When the coordinator checkout is a linked worktree (a supported install mode per the repo's own worktree-install flow), <root>/.git is a pointer file: all shared re-binds resolve under a file and vanish, and the true common Git directory lies outside root, so --ro-bind root root never covers it while --dev-bind / / leaves it writable — a confined session can git -C <coordinator> commit --allow-empty and move the coordinator branch, voiding GY-888's guarantee. Not already fixed: the code exists only on the PR branch (origin/main has neither readOnlyMountWrapper nor sessionGitAdminDirectory) and thread PRRT_kwDOUZby-s6m_HFI (r4130348375) was resolved by a reply naming this item, not by code. Not mergeable into GY-888: the reviewer approved it with all criteria met and judged this finding beyond the item's criteria, matching the repo's follow-up-item convention (GY-936, GY-940, GY-952). Priority 1: P1 severity on a supported deployment path, actionable as GY-888 lands since the vulnerable code is not yet on main.

work.title: A pipeline-doctor agent runs every 10 minutes, finds stuck and overdue work, and fixes it through sanctioned commands, doing what the master has done by hand all day

criteria.text: A 'doctor' agent role, implemented in a new module this item creates (src/daemon/doctor.ts), (registry and profile role, headless on Pi by default with a strong-model fallback, like the diagnostician) is launched by the loop every 10 minutes (configurable, run.doctor.intervalMinutes) with the master's read access and the operator-agent identity's sanctioned commands only (master scope, requirements, unblock, decide + approver, settle-containment, close, create/release), never merge, dispatch, evidence or lease commands. Its prompt is a shipped template (not this repository's session prompts) listing the checks and fault bounds: blocked > 10 min, worker > 60 min, CI > 20 min, review request > 5 min after green CI, launch > 2 min, proofs > 30 min, mergeable > 5 min, unanswered decision > 10 min, lapsed containment, stale refusal text, items overdue in any step. A test asserts the schedule, the role's command allowlist (a refused command is recorded, not run) and that the template names every bound.

Each doctor run records its findings and actions as an event per item and one run summary (what was stuck, why, what it did, what it filed), visible in master status and on the dashboard (a 'Doctor' panel with the last runs). A finding it cannot act on (a human-only decision, a fault class with no item) raises attention or files a P0/P1 fault item with criteria and plannedFiles, deduplicated against open items. A test asserts the event, the summary and the dedup.

The deterministic remedies the doctor applies most often are also performed by the loop itself without an agent: settle a lapsed containment whose attempt submitted; clear a blocker whose named scope is already in plannedFiles; relaunch an approver for a decision unanswered past 10 minutes. The doctor handles what needs judgement. A test asserts each automatic remedy.

docs/master-agent.md and docs/onboarding.md state the doctor role, its schedule, its command allowlist and how an installation turns it off, within the docs word budget; onboarding enables it by default.

work.title: Review, rework and proof launches require a GitHub observation under two minutes old, which the observation workers rarely supply, so items wait hours for a reviewer

criteria.text: A review, producer or approver launch requires only that the item's latest observation is of the request's exact head and base (no age bound); if the head or base has moved since, the request is superseded as today. The two-minute bound stays for merge authorization. A test with a 20-minute-old observation of the requested head asserts the review launches, and one of a moved head asserts it does not.

Where a fresh observation is genuinely required (merge, rework of a possibly-moved head), the requesting step wakes that item's observation job with priority immediately after the refusal, and the next attempt happens after that observation lands rather than on a fixed retry. A test asserts the wake and that the second attempt follows the observation.
master status reports, per waiting launch, how long it has waited and why; a review request waiting over 15 minutes raises an attention item. A test asserts it.

work.title: OpenCode sessions never count as started: the start pattern /\bOpenCode\b/ never matches OpenCode 1.18's screen, so every OpenCode launch times out and silently falls back to Claude

criteria.text: The OpenCode start check in src/master/launch.ts recognizes OpenCode 1.18's start screen: the TUI's own elements, such as the input prompt or hint bar ('tab agents' / 'ctrl+' hints) or the logo drawn in box characters, and not the echoed launch command line, which also contains the lowercase word opencode. A test in tests/runtime-screens.test.ts feeds a recorded OpenCode 1.18 start screen (captured as a fixture) and asserts 'ready', and feeds the bare echoed launch command and asserts it is not ready.

When a launch falls back to another account after the preferred account's runtime failed to start, the dispatch record and master status name both (for example 'opencode-a failed to start: <reason>; launched on claude-b'), and three consecutive start failures of one account raise one attention item naming the account and runtime, so a runtime that never starts is visible rather than silently replaced. A test asserts the record, and that the attention item appears after three failures.

work.title: A CI failure on a speculative queue tip is blamed on the entry under test, not the predecessor that caused it

criteria.text: When a required check fails on a speculative queue tip, the loop attributes the failure before requesting any rework. It compares the files named by the failing test output, and the failing test's subject, against the diff of the entry and of each predecessor in the tip. When a predecessor's own head fails the same check, or its diff contains the named file and the entry's does not, the predecessor is ejected with the failure named, the entry is re-queued, and no rework is requested for the entry. Only a failure attributable to the entry's own diff, or one that no predecessor explains, requests the entry's rework. A test replays the GY-392/GY-422 case and asserts that GY-422 is ejected and GY-392 re-queued with no rework decision.
Every CI-failure rework request on a queue tip names the tip's predecessors and the attribution evidence, so an approver can verify it. A test asserts the request text.

work.title: Automatic reviews run in parallel and never stall on one stale reviewer name: the review profile defaults to several sessions and a finished reviewer releases its name

criteria.text: With run.reviewerProfile set and that profile's concurrency unset, automatic review launches can run more than one session at once (a documented default above 1, or rotation across the configured reviewer profiles); a test launches three concurrent review requests and none is refused for the agent-name bound.

A reviewer session whose review request has settled (verdict posted, request satisfied or superseded) is closed and its agent name released within one loop cycle; a test leaves a settled reviewer idle in its pane and shows the next review launch succeeds on that name.
`npm run build` and `npm test` pass; docs describe the reviewer concurrency default.

work.title: OpenCode sessions never count as started: the start pattern /\bOpenCode\b/ never matches OpenCode 1.18's screen, so every OpenCode launch times out and silently falls back to Claude

criteria.text: The OpenCode start check in src/master/launch.ts recognizes OpenCode 1.18's start screen: the TUI's own elements, such as the input prompt or hint bar ('tab agents' / 'ctrl+' hints) or the logo drawn in box characters, and not the echoed launch command line, which also contains the lowercase word opencode. A test in tests/runtime-screens.test.ts feeds a recorded OpenCode 1.18 start screen (captured as a fixture) and asserts 'ready', and feeds the bare echoed launch command and asserts it is not ready.

When a launch falls back to another account after the preferred account's runtime failed to start, the dispatch record and master status name both (for example 'opencode-a failed to start: <reason>; launched on claude-b'), and three consecutive start failures of one account raise one attention item naming the account and runtime, so a runtime that never starts is visible rather than silently replaced. A test asserts the record, and that the attention item appears after three failures.

in dispatchWork (src/master/dispatch.ts) the SessionStartError catch no longer records the account start failure (recordAccountStartFailure / startFailures.push) and falls back to the next account; it rethrows instead

work.title: GitHub API use fits the rate limit: cache immutable reads, share per-cycle reads, observe on webhooks

criteria.text: Reads of immutable GitHub objects are cached permanently in the GitHub cache: a commit by SHA and a compare between two exact SHAs are fetched at most once. A test replays two observation cycles over the same SHAs and asserts the second makes no request for them.

The base branch ref and its protection are read once per cycle (protection at most every 5 minutes or on a branch_protection_rule/repository webhook) and shared by every item's check. A test observing 20 items in one cycle asserts one ref read and at most one protection read.

GitHub webhooks drive observation: a pull_request, pull_request_review, check_run, check_suite or push event marks the affected items' observation jobs due at once, ahead of polled jobs, and polling of an item a webhook refreshed within its poll interval is skipped. A test delivers a check_run event and asserts the item is re-observed without waiting for its poll, and that the poll that follows is skipped.

master status reports billable GitHub requests per hour against the budget, by endpoint, and a replay of the 2026-09-26 workload (the recorded request mix) stays under 60% of one token's hourly limit. A test asserts the projection. The item creates tests/github-budget.test.ts for these tests.

exercise.behaviour: the immutableRead dispatch in GitHub.apiRequest (if GET && immutableRead(path) return this.immutableRequest(path)) removed, so commits by SHA and exact compares go through the ETag path
cycleBaseBranch stubbed to return readBaseBranch() and sharedProtectionRead stubbed to return request(path): no per-cycle sharing of base ref or protection reads
takeJob webhook_at -1 claim priority removed and processJob poll-skip (if refreshedUntil !== null deferJob) disabled
billable report removed: billable field of GitHub.budget(), chargeLedger.charge in record(), billable in observationThroughputStatus

work.title: Concurrent agent test runs exhaust host memory: the loop launches sessions with no bound on full-suite and typecheck runs per machine

criteria.text: Heavy verification commands run under a per-host concurrency bound: `npm test`, `npm run test:browser` and `tsc --noEmit` launched by Graphyard sessions (worker, producer, reviewer) take a slot from a host-wide semaphore (a lock directory under the managed worktree root, default slots = max(2, floor(total memory GB / 8)), configurable per host) and wait for a free slot, printing that they wait and on what. Implemented as a wrapper the session harness puts on PATH for those commands (or the test runner itself acquiring the slot). A test starts more runs than slots and asserts no more than the bound run at once and the rest complete after.

Dispatch and producer launches consult host memory: when available memory is below a product default (10% of total or 4 GB, whichever is larger) the loop defers new launches on that host with a recorded reason, raises one `resources` attention item naming the top memory consumers, and resumes once memory recovers. A test with a stubbed memory reading asserts the deferral, the attention and the resumption.
docs/operations-reference.md states the slot bound, its setting and the memory deferral within the docs word budget.

work.title: A pipeline-doctor agent runs every 10 minutes, finds stuck and overdue work, and fixes it through sanctioned commands, doing what the master has done by hand all day

criteria.text: A 'doctor' agent role, implemented in a new module this item creates (src/daemon/doctor.ts), (registry and profile role, headless on Pi by default with a strong-model fallback, like the diagnostician) is launched by the loop every 10 minutes (configurable, run.doctor.intervalMinutes) with the master's read access and the operator-agent identity's sanctioned commands only (master scope, requirements, unblock, decide + approver, settle-containment, close, create/release), never merge, dispatch, evidence or lease commands. Its prompt is a shipped template (not this repository's session prompts) listing the checks and fault bounds: blocked > 10 min, worker > 60 min, CI > 20 min, review request > 5 min after green CI, launch > 2 min, proofs > 30 min, mergeable > 5 min, unanswered decision > 10 min, lapsed containment, stale refusal text, items overdue in any step. A test asserts the schedule, the role's command allowlist (a refused command is recorded, not run) and that the template names every bound.

Each doctor run records its findings and actions as an event per item and one run summary (what was stuck, why, what it did, what it filed), visible in master status and on the dashboard (a 'Doctor' panel with the last runs). A finding it cannot act on (a human-only decision, a fault class with no item) raises attention or files a P0/P1 fault item with criteria and plannedFiles, deduplicated against open items. A test asserts the event, the summary and the dedup.

The deterministic remedies the doctor applies most often are also performed by the loop itself without an agent: settle a lapsed containment whose attempt submitted; clear a blocker whose named scope is already in plannedFiles; relaunch an approver for a decision unanswered past 10 minutes. The doctor handles what needs judgement. A test asserts each automatic remedy.

docs/master-agent.md and docs/onboarding.md state the doctor role, its schedule, its command allowlist and how an installation turns it off, within the docs word budget; onboarding enables it by default.

work.title: A CI failure on a speculative queue tip is blamed on the entry under test, not the predecessor that caused it

criteria.text: When a required check fails on a speculative queue tip, the loop attributes the failure before requesting any rework. It compares the files named by the failing test output, and the failing test's subject, against the diff of the entry and of each predecessor in the tip. When a predecessor's own head fails the same check, or its diff contains the named file and the entry's does not, the predecessor is ejected with the failure named, the entry is re-queued, and no rework is requested for the entry. Only a failure attributable to the entry's own diff, or one that no predecessor explains, requests the entry's rework. A test replays the GY-392/GY-422 case and asserts that GY-422 is ejected and GY-392 re-queued with no rework decision.
Every CI-failure rework request on a queue tip names the tip's predecessors and the attribution evidence, so an approver can verify it. A test asserts the request text.

work.title: OpenCode sessions never count as started: the start pattern /\bOpenCode\b/ never matches OpenCode 1.18's screen, so every OpenCode launch times out and silently falls back to Claude

criteria.text: The OpenCode start check in src/master/launch.ts recognizes OpenCode 1.18's start screen: the TUI's own elements, such as the input prompt or hint bar ('tab agents' / 'ctrl+' hints) or the logo drawn in box characters, and not the echoed launch command line, which also contains the lowercase word opencode. A test in tests/runtime-screens.test.ts feeds a recorded OpenCode 1.18 start screen (captured as a fixture) and asserts 'ready', and feeds the bare echoed launch command and asserts it is not ready.

When a launch falls back to another account after the preferred account's runtime failed to start, the dispatch record and master status name both (for example 'opencode-a failed to start: <reason>; launched on claude-b'), and three consecutive start failures of one account raise one attention item naming the account and runtime, so a runtime that never starts is visible rather than silently replaced. A test asserts the record, and that the attention item appears after three failures.

work.title: Review, rework and proof launches require a GitHub observation under two minutes old, which the observation workers rarely supply, so items wait hours for a reviewer

criteria.text: A review, producer or approver launch requires only that the item's latest observation is of the request's exact head and base (no age bound); if the head or base has moved since, the request is superseded as today. The two-minute bound stays for merge authorization. A test with a 20-minute-old observation of the requested head asserts the review launches, and one of a moved head asserts it does not.

Where a fresh observation is genuinely required (merge, rework of a possibly-moved head), the requesting step wakes that item's observation job with priority immediately after the refusal, and the next attempt happens after that observation lands rather than on a fixed retry. A test asserts the wake and that the second attempt follows the observation.
master status reports, per waiting launch, how long it has waited and why; a review request waiting over 15 minutes raises an attention item. A test asserts it.

work.title: A new attempt's worktree never fails because an earlier attempt's worktree still holds the branch

criteria.text: Worktree allocation for a new attempt that finds the item's branch held by an earlier attempt's worktree (checked out, or mid rebase, merge or cherry-pick) records that worktree's refs and uncommitted diff under the item's preserved-attempt record, ends the in-progress operation, detaches that worktree's HEAD, and then creates the new worktree; the branch ref never moves. A test leaves a rebase in progress on the branch in an old attempt's worktree and asserts the next allocation succeeds with the branch at its prior commit and the old state recorded.

A dispatch that fails for a host-side reason about the item's own workspace (not the profile) neither advances the attempt epoch nor puts the profile into its failure cool-off; the failure is recorded on the item with the git message. The item creates tests/worktree-branch-lock.test.ts for these tests.

work.title: GitHub API use fits the rate limit: cache immutable reads, share per-cycle reads, observe on webhooks

criteria.text: Reads of immutable GitHub objects are cached permanently in the GitHub cache: a commit by SHA and a compare between two exact SHAs are fetched at most once. A test replays two observation cycles over the same SHAs and asserts the second makes no request for them.

The base branch ref and its protection are read once per cycle (protection at most every 5 minutes or on a branch_protection_rule/repository webhook) and shared by every item's check. A test observing 20 items in one cycle asserts one ref read and at most one protection read.

GitHub webhooks drive observation: a pull_request, pull_request_review, check_run, check_suite or push event marks the affected items' observation jobs due at once, ahead of polled jobs, and polling of an item a webhook refreshed within its poll interval is skipped. A test delivers a check_run event and asserts the item is re-observed without waiting for its poll, and that the poll that follows is skipped.

master status reports billable GitHub requests per hour against the budget, by endpoint, and a replay of the 2026-09-26 workload (the recorded request mix) stays under 60% of one token's hourly limit. A test asserts the projection. The item creates tests/github-budget.test.ts for these tests.

exercise.behaviour: the immutableRead dispatch in GitHub.apiRequest (if GET && immutableRead(path) return this.immutableRequest(path)) removed, so commits by SHA and exact compares go through the ETag path
cycleBaseBranch stubbed to return readBaseBranch() and sharedProtectionRead stubbed to return request(path): no per-cycle sharing of base ref or protection reads
takeJob webhook_at -1 claim priority removed and processJob poll-skip (if refreshedUntil !== null deferJob) disabled
billable report removed: billable field of GitHub.budget(), chargeLedger.charge in record(), billable in observationThroughputStatus

work.title: OpenCode sessions never count as started: the start pattern /\bOpenCode\b/ never matches OpenCode 1.18's screen, so every OpenCode launch times out and silently falls back to Claude

criteria.text: The OpenCode start check in src/master/launch.ts recognizes OpenCode 1.18's start screen: the TUI's own elements, such as the input prompt or hint bar ('tab agents' / 'ctrl+' hints) or the logo drawn in box characters, and not the echoed launch command line, which also contains the lowercase word opencode. A test in tests/runtime-screens.test.ts feeds a recorded OpenCode 1.18 start screen (captured as a fixture) and asserts 'ready', and feeds the bare echoed launch command and asserts it is not ready.

When a launch falls back to another account after the preferred account's runtime failed to start, the dispatch record and master status name both (for example 'opencode-a failed to start: <reason>; launched on claude-b'), and three consecutive start failures of one account raise one attention item naming the account and runtime, so a runtime that never starts is visible rather than silently replaced. A test asserts the record, and that the attention item appears after three failures.

exercise.behaviour: runtimeScreens.opencode in src/master/launch.ts reverted from /\btab agents\b|Ask anything…/ to the old /\bOpenCode\b/

in dispatchWork (src/master/dispatch.ts) the SessionStartError catch no longer records the account start failure (recordAccountStartFailure / startFailures.push) and falls back to the next account; it rethrows instead

work.title: Automatic reviews run in parallel and never stall on one stale reviewer name: the review profile defaults to several sessions and a finished reviewer releases its name

criteria.text: With run.reviewerProfile set and that profile's concurrency unset, automatic review launches can run more than one session at once (a documented default above 1, or rotation across the configured reviewer profiles); a test launches three concurrent review requests and none is refused for the agent-name bound.

A reviewer session whose review request has settled (verdict posted, request satisfied or superseded) is closed and its agent name released within one loop cycle; a test leaves a settled reviewer idle in its pane and shows the next review launch succeeds on that name.
`npm run build` and `npm test` pass; docs describe the reviewer concurrency default.

work.title: Reviewer, producer and approver sessions start in their own managed checkout, never in the coordinator checkout

criteria.text: Every session Graphyard launches for a role other than the master (reviewer, producer, approver, escalation handler, research, triage) is started with its pane cwd and process cwd set to its own managed checkout (or, for sessions with no checkout, a scratch directory outside the coordinator checkout); no launch passes the coordinator checkout as a cwd. A test builds each role's launch and asserts the cwd is outside the coordinator checkout and equals the session's checkout where it has one.

The loop checks the coordinator checkout each cycle: when HEAD is not the commit it runs or the tree is dirty, it records attention naming the paths, the HEAD and the sessions whose checkouts or panes point at it, and does not self-upgrade or restart from it until it is clean. The item creates tests/session-cwd.test.ts for these tests.

in coordinatorCheckoutGuard (src/daemon/run.ts) headDrift stubbed to false, pointingSessions stubbed to return [], and betweenCycles reads the checkout only when a selfUpgrade is due

work.title: A new attempt's worktree never fails because an earlier attempt's worktree still holds the branch

criteria.text: Worktree allocation for a new attempt that finds the item's branch held by an earlier attempt's worktree (checked out, or mid rebase, merge or cherry-pick) records that worktree's refs and uncommitted diff under the item's preserved-attempt record, ends the in-progress operation, detaches that worktree's HEAD, and then creates the new worktree; the branch ref never moves. A test leaves a rebase in progress on the branch in an old attempt's worktree and asserts the next allocation succeeds with the branch at its prior commit and the old state recorded.

A dispatch that fails for a host-side reason about the item's own workspace (not the profile) neither advances the attempt epoch nor puts the profile into its failure cool-off; the failure is recorded on the item with the git message. The item creates tests/worktree-branch-lock.test.ts for these tests.

exercise.behaviour: releaseHeldBranch in src/master/worktrees.ts stubbed to register(null) and return null at entry, so no held worktree is preserved, ended or detached
engine release no longer undoes the untouched workspace-failed claim (epoch not returned) and workspaceDispatchFailure in src/master/dispatch.ts always false, so the profile is cooled off

work.title: Most merge-queue conflicts are in a handful of shared docs pages, so every merge on main sends queued items back to a full worker rework

criteria.text: A candidate whose conflicts with the base are confined to docs/**/*.md is refreshed by the control plane, not reworked: a short docs-sync session (reviewer-class account, narrow prompt: merge the base, keep both sides' meaning, stay within the word budget, touch only the conflicted docs paragraphs) resolves it on the item's branch, the docs obligation check and word-budget test rerun, and the item keeps its approval when the non-docs diff (patch-id of paths outside docs/) is unchanged. A test asserts: a docs-only conflict leads to a docs-sync session and no rework decision; a conflict touching src/ still goes to rework; approval kept when the non-docs patch is unchanged.

master status and Insights report conflict hotspots: the paths most often conflicting in the last 24 hours with counts and the items they sent back, and raise an attention item when one path causes 5 or more conflicts in 24 hours. A test asserts the report.

docs/development.md states how to document a change so it rarely conflicts (add a self-contained paragraph or section rather than rewording shared sentences) and the docs-sync rule, within the docs word budget.

conflictHotspots in src/model/conflict-hotspots.ts no longer aggregates conflicts per path (per-path loop emptied), so no hotspots or attention are reported

criteria.text: When a candidate passes every gate except one or more manual: proofs that no configured producer may run (the proof is not in producerProofs and no producer request exists for it), the loop requests one attestation decision per such proof, naming the proof, the exact head, base and policy revision, and launches an independent approver for it, within one cycle, exactly as it requests merge decisions. work.title: OpenCode sessions never count as started: the start pattern /\bOpenCode\b/ never matches OpenCode 1.18's screen, so every OpenCode launch times out and silently falls back to Claude

criteria.text: The OpenCode start check in src/master/launch.ts recognizes OpenCode 1.18's start screen: the TUI's own elements, such as the input prompt or hint bar ('tab agents' / 'ctrl+' hints) or the logo drawn in box characters, and not the echoed launch command line, which also contains the lowercase word opencode. A test in tests/runtime-screens.test.ts feeds a recorded OpenCode 1.18 start screen (captured as a fixture) and asserts 'ready', and feeds the bare echoed launch command and asserts it is not ready.

When a launch falls back to another account after the preferred account's runtime failed to start, the dispatch record and master status name both (for example 'opencode-a failed to start: <reason>; launched on claude-b'), and three consecutive start failures of one account raise one attention item naming the account and runtime, so a runtime that never starts is visible rather than silently replaced. A test asserts the record, and that the attention item appears after three failures.

in dispatchWork (src/master/dispatch.ts) the SessionStartError catch no longer records the account start failure (recordAccountStartFailure / startFailures.push) and falls back to the next account; it rethrows instead

work.title: Candidates whose CI failed only from a since-fixed base-branch breakage are refreshed onto main automatically

criteria.text: When a candidate's required check fails and every failing test also fails on the base branch commit it was built against, while that test passes on the current base tip, the loop refreshes the candidate onto the base tip (the same refresh the merge queue uses, keeping approvals and proofs the refresh policy keeps) instead of requesting rework, and records why. A test builds this history (a failing test on the old base, fixed on the new tip) and asserts the refresh with no rework decision. The item creates src/master/base-break-refresh.ts for this detection and tests/base-break-refresh.test.ts for its tests.

A decision step gated on a fresh GitHub observation wakes that item's observation job itself and is re-evaluated as soon as the reading lands, so the freshness bound is met rather than missed on every cycle. A test asserts that a waiting rework decision proceeds within one observation after the wake, not on the next unrelated cycle.

master status names a candidate held only by a base-branch breakage as such (the failing test, the base commit that broke it and the one that fixed it), not as 'needs a new head'. A test asserts the wording.

work.title: Reviewer, producer and approver sessions start in their own managed checkout, never in the coordinator checkout

criteria.text: Every session Graphyard launches for a role other than the master (reviewer, producer, approver, escalation handler, research, triage) is started with its pane cwd and process cwd set to its own managed checkout (or, for sessions with no checkout, a scratch directory outside the coordinator checkout); no launch passes the coordinator checkout as a cwd. A test builds each role's launch and asserts the cwd is outside the coordinator checkout and equals the session's checkout where it has one.

The loop checks the coordinator checkout each cycle: when HEAD is not the commit it runs or the tree is dirty, it records attention naming the paths, the HEAD and the sessions whose checkouts or panes point at it, and does not self-upgrade or restart from it until it is clean. The item creates tests/session-cwd.test.ts for these tests.

work.title: Review follow-ups stay on their parent until it ships, and only then become work items

criteria.text: An approval's follow-up findings on an unshipped parent are recorded on the parent (listed on its page and in master status as pending follow-ups), not filed as a work item; when the parent is delivered, one follow-up item is created from the findings still standing, depending on nothing. A test approves a parent with findings, asserts no item exists, delivers the parent, and asserts one item with those findings.

A one-time migration folds each open follow-up item whose parent has not shipped back onto its parent and closes it as superseded by the parent, deleting nothing; a parent closed without shipping drops its pending follow-ups with a recorded reason. A test covers both.
Triage never judges a follow-up whose parent has not shipped. The item creates tests/followups-after-ship.test.ts for these tests.

A parent never has more than one open follow-up item in any stage: a later approval of a parent whose follow-up item is already open (released, in build or beyond) appends its new findings to that item, deduplicated, instead of filing another. On 2026-09-26 re-approvals during rework filed 48 duplicates across 29 parents (GY-430 got GY-730, GY-734 and GY-753 in 80 minutes). A test approves a parent three times with its follow-up item released between approvals and asserts one open follow-up item holding the union of findings.

work.title: Review follow-ups stay on their parent until it ships, and only then become work items

criteria.text: An approval's follow-up findings on an unshipped parent are recorded on the parent (listed on its page and in master status as pending follow-ups), not filed as a work item; when the parent is delivered, one follow-up item is created from the findings still standing, depending on nothing. A test approves a parent with findings, asserts no item exists, delivers the parent, and asserts one item with those findings.

A one-time migration folds each open follow-up item whose parent has not shipped back onto its parent and closes it as superseded by the parent, deleting nothing; a parent closed without shipping drops its pending follow-ups with a recorded reason. A test covers both.
Triage never judges a follow-up whose parent has not shipped. The item creates tests/followups-after-ship.test.ts for these tests.

A parent never has more than one open follow-up item in any stage: a later approval of a parent whose follow-up item is already open (released, in build or beyond) appends its new findings to that item, deduplicated, instead of filing another. On 2026-09-26 re-approvals during rework filed 48 duplicates across 29 parents (GY-430 got GY-730, GY-734 and GY-753 in 80 minutes). A test approves a parent three times with its follow-up item released between approvals and asserts one open follow-up item holding the union of findings.

work.title: Automatic quarantine settlement bounds the clock with a fast read, not the slow snapshot

criteria.text: Before assessing containment, the loop measures its clock offset against the control plane with a light timed read whose round trip bounds the offset (the server's time from a small endpoint, or the Date of a cheap request), and passes those bounds to the assessment instead of the snapshot read's. A test with a 12-second snapshot read and a 200 ms timed read asserts a lapsed, verified-dead quarantine is settled automatically.

When the light read itself cannot bound the offset within tolerance, the refusal names the measured round trip, and master status says settlement waits on a faster control-plane read rather than on a clock disagreement. A test asserts the wording.

work.title: Follow-ups from the approved review of GY-888 (PR #455)

judgement.reason: Real, unfixed P1 containment hole. At PR #455's head d13fee0482 (= the approved review commit; no later code change), src/master/profiles.ts:650 readOnlyMountWrapper hard-codes gitDir = join(root, '.git') and drops every shared re-bind that is not a directory (.filter(isDirectoryPath)); runtimeSandboxConfines (line 572) and sessionGitAdminDirectory share the assumption. When the coordinator checkout is a linked worktree (a supported install mode per the repo's own worktree-install flow), <root>/.git is a pointer file: all shared re-binds resolve under a file and vanish, and the true common Git directory lies outside root, so --ro-bind root root never covers it while --dev-bind / / leaves it writable — a confined session can git -C <coordinator> commit --allow-empty and move the coordinator branch, voiding GY-888's guarantee. Not already fixed: the code exists only on the PR branch (origin/main has neither readOnlyMountWrapper nor sessionGitAdminDirectory) and thread PRRT_kwDOUZby-s6m_HFI (r4130348375) was resolved by a reply naming this item, not by code. Not mergeable into GY-888: the reviewer approved it with all criteria met and judged this finding beyond the item's criteria, matching the repo's follow-up-item convention (GY-936, GY-940, GY-952). Priority 1: P1 severity on a supported deployment path, actionable as GY-888 lands since the vulnerable code is not yet on main.

work.title: Review follow-ups stay on their parent until it ships, and only then become work items

criteria.text: An approval's follow-up findings on an unshipped parent are recorded on the parent (listed on its page and in master status as pending follow-ups), not filed as a work item; when the parent is delivered, one follow-up item is created from the findings still standing, depending on nothing. A test approves a parent with findings, asserts no item exists, delivers the parent, and asserts one item with those findings.

A one-time migration folds each open follow-up item whose parent has not shipped back onto its parent and closes it as superseded by the parent, deleting nothing; a parent closed without shipping drops its pending follow-ups with a recorded reason. A test covers both.
Triage never judges a follow-up whose parent has not shipped. The item creates tests/followups-after-ship.test.ts for these tests.

A parent never has more than one open follow-up item in any stage: a later approval of a parent whose follow-up item is already open (released, in build or beyond) appends its new findings to that item, deduplicated, instead of filing another. On 2026-09-26 re-approvals during rework filed 48 duplicates across 29 parents (GY-430 got GY-730, GY-734 and GY-753 in 80 minutes). A test approves a parent three times with its follow-up item released between approvals and asserts one open follow-up item holding the union of findings.

work.title: Coordination writes stop reading every work item's full document while holding the global lock, so claims, selections and renewals no longer queue for seconds

criteria.text: No code path that holds the coordination advisory lock issues an unbounded `SELECT document FROM work_items` (with or without ORDER BY/FOR UPDATE); a test scans the source for such queries inside transaction callbacks and fails on any, and each former call site reads only the item, its overlapping open items and its dependencies.

A benchmark test with 1000 work items (600 closed, each with a realistic document) shows claim, renew, submit and agent-registry select each complete in under 500 ms of lock hold time, and their duration does not grow with the number of closed items.

Planned-file overlap, exclusive-resource conflicts, dependency readiness and delivered settlement give the same answers as before on the existing tests; `npm run build` and `npm test` pass; docs/operations describe the bound.

Merge f85d453acf first (local branch prodfix/secrets-bus, shared by this host's repository; it carries the live sandbox fixes too): registry requests use fleetRequestTimeoutMs, 30 s, instead of a 10 s bound that abandoned selections queued behind the lock.
Merge 251097c765 (it contains f85d453acf): heldAwareProbe and every other registry client use fleetRequestTimeoutMs, and a test refuses a literal timeout passed to httpFleetClient anywhere in src/.

Engine.reconcile (src/engine.ts ~2075) no longer re-reads every full document per batch under the lock: on 2026-10-01 each batch spent 15-19 s reading and parsing ~1000 documents for 1 s of work, so the lock was held almost continuously (GRAPHYARD_RECONCILE_BATCH_MS was raised to 5000 as a stopgap). A batch reads its own open rows plus a compact projection of the rest, its lock hold including the read stays within the batch budget, and a test with 1000 items (600 closed) shows a full pass holds the lock under 5 s in total.

exercise.behaviour: Engine.execute reads the whole board again (SELECT document FROM work_items ORDER BY number) instead of lockedWork(db, [id])
lockedRows reads every row whole (readWhole over all listed rows) instead of focus + own rows with stand-ins for the rest
each reconcile batch reads every work item whole (SELECT number, document FROM work_items) instead of lockedRows(db, [], {after: cursor, limit})
fleetRequestTimeoutMs set back to the old 10_000 ms registry request bound
